subject: Priority alignment + competitor clarifications — Redwood demo follow-up
messages:
From: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@medidex.com>, Emily Park <emily.park@medidex.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 9 Jul 2027 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Priority alignment + competitor clarifications — Redwood demo follow-up

Thanks again for your time today — really appreciated the candid discussion. Quick recap so we’re aligned and don’t miss any asks. Please flag anything I missed.

High-level goals you shared:
- Replace current inference stack to reduce per-token costs and improve tail latency for multi-turn clinical summarization flows.
- Maintain / improve hallucination profile for structured outputs (ICD codes, dosages).
- Achieve predictable SLA for peak clinic hours (Pacific US).

Primary pain points:
1) Unpredictable 99th percentile latency on batches during the 8–10am spike.
2) Tokenization/formatting drift when vendors rebase models (breaking ICD formatting).
3) Auditability — need per-request logs and retention controls for 12 months.

Decision criteria (weighted by your team roughly):
- Latency (50%) — 99th P and P95 under load
- Output fidelity (30%) — structured extraction accuracy on our labeled prompt set
- Cost predictability (20%) — committed vs burst pricing options

Competitive snapshot discussed (for clarity):
- OrbitAI: good throughput, weaker gating on structured outputs
- NimbusAI: strong accuracy but higher fixed cost for reserved nodes
- Large public cloud endpoint: flexible but noisy tail latency in your tests

Open questions / asks from your side:
- Can we run a 1-hour head-to-head with our 2k-token clinical transcripts at your cluster? You noted interest in seeing 99th percentile under sustained load.
- SOC 2 scope and per-request log retention — Emily asked about retention + export options.
- Procurement timeline: you mentioned internal stakeholders want a redline-ready term sheet by 7/20.

Proposed next steps (my suggestions):
1) I’ll share the demo recording and a concise comparison matrix (attached).
2) Karthik to coordinate environment details and start a perf run next week (requesting test dataset and expected QPS).
3) We’ll schedule a 60-min perf kickoff with your SREs — propose Mon 7/12 or Tue 7/13, Calendly link below.
4) I’ll also attach a short SOC2 summary; if you need the auditor contact, I’ll pull that today.

Attachments: MediDex_Matrix_Comparison.xlsx (matrix + quick notes)

Thanks — will follow up after Karthik confirms perf windows.

—
Avery Johnson
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Priority alignment + competitor clarifications — Redwood demo follow-up

Thanks, Avery — helpful recap. A couple clarifications from our side: 

1) Perf test scope: we want a sustained 30 QPS run for 60 minutes with the full 2,048 token window and the clinical prompt set (we’ll send the anonymized transcripts). The key metric is 99th percentile latency and memory behavior when KV cache grows. If you can log per-request KV sizes, that would be ideal.

2) SOC2: Emily — can you confirm that Redwood can provide an auditor contact and a redacted SOC2 report within 48 hours? We’ll need to pull that into the security pack for our GRC team.

3) Procurement timeline: procurement is targeting a LOI by 7/22. We need an estimate for committed capacity pricing vs burst pricing to model TCO.

We are happy to run the head-to-head; send the perf harness instructions and a rough ETA and we’ll slot SRE time.

Appreciate the quick responses, Sanjay. Confirming next steps and logistics below so we have a single source of truth: 

1) Perf kickoff: proposed Mon 12 Jul 09:00 PT — Karthik will send a short runbook and the harness (locust + scripts). We’ll ask you to drop the anonymized 2k-token transcripts to the secure S3 link we’ll provide.

2) Metrics we’ll collect and share: P95/P99 latency, p50/p90, per-request KV size, memory headroom, and sample response fidelity for the structured-output tests. Results in CSV + Grafana snapshot.

3) SOC2 & security: Marissa will send a redacted SOC2 pdf (SOC2-summary.pdf) and auditor contact by EOD 7/10. If GRC needs anything extra, please loop Emily and we’ll escalate.

4) Pricing sketch: I’ll send a two-line pricing sketch for committed vs burst tiers by 7/12 morning so procurement can model TCO for the LOI.

5) Calendly: here’s a booking link if the proposed kickoff doesn’t work — https://calendly.com/avery-j/30min.

If that all looks good, I’ll lock the kickoff and Karthik will reach out with the runbook.

Thanks — looking forward to the head-to-head.
